title: The India Story Trailer Drops: Shreyas Talpade and Kajal Aggarwal Take On the Pesticide Crisis
excerpt: The hard-hitting courtroom drama about food adulteration and pesticide farming releases in cinemas on July 24 across Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.
body:
• The official trailer for The India Story: Slow Poison in Progress has been released, starring Kajal Aggarwal and Shreyas Talpade.
  • The film is a courtroom drama centered on pesticide farming, food adulteration and their impact on public health in India.
  • Directed by Chettan DK and produced by Sagar B Shinde under Zee Studios, it releases on July 24 in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.
  • Talpade plays a grieving father who takes on the food and agro-chemical industry; Aggarwal plays the lawyer fighting alongside him.

A Film That Wants to Make You Uncomfortable

In a Bollywood season dominated by action spectacles and franchise sequels, The India Story is deliberately counterprogramming. The trailer, released on July 18 by Zee Studios, opens with a father's grief and builds into a furious indictment of India's food adulteration crisis.

Shreyas Talpade, best known for comedic roles, sheds that skin entirely. He plays a man who loses his daughter to cancer and traces the cause back to the pesticide-laden food supply chain. His character's crusade against the agro-chemical industry forms the film's central conflict.

Kajal Aggarwal — credited as Kajal A Kitchlu — plays a lawyer who takes up the legal battle. The trailer shows their courtroom confrontation with powerful corporate interests, with Talpade's character challenging a system that calls farmers terrorists while poisoning the food they grow.

"It's a story of an ordinary man's fight against an extraordinary challenge, driven by hope and determination."

— Shreyas Talpade, actor

The Team Behind the Film

The India Story is directed by Chettan DK and written and produced by Sagar B Shinde. The supporting cast includes Murli Sharma, Manish Wadhwa, Atul Tiwari and Kamlesh Sawant. Technical credits include cinematographer Nishant Bhagwat, music director Mangesh Dhakde and editor Ashish Mhatre.

Director Chettan DK described the project as "more than just a film." Speaking to media, he said the team wanted to "shine a light on an issue that silently impacts every household" and hopes the trailer inspires audiences to "question, reflect, and engage with the reality around them."

Why It Matters

India's pesticide use has been a persistent public health concern. The country is one of the world's largest consumers of agricultural pesticides, and studies have linked long-term exposure to elevated cancer rates, neurological damage and soil degradation. Despite regulations, enforcement remains inconsistent, and adulteration of food products — from milk to spices — regularly makes headlines.

For the Indian diaspora, food safety is a conversation that bridges continents. Many NRI families regularly discuss the quality of food in India, and concerns about pesticide residue in imported Indian goods have grown in recent years. A mainstream Bollywood film tackling the subject could amplify awareness in ways that policy reports and newspaper investigations have not.

Release Details

The India Story: Slow Poison in Progress opens in cinemas worldwide on July 24, 2026, in three languages: Hindi, Tamil and Telugu. A social media campaign around the hashtag #WhatsOnYourPlate has been running ahead of the release.
